notes.text: The 12 V supply, from outside the board: 9 V to 16 V.
The input after the reverse-polarity diode.
The 5 V rail, made by the first buck stage and the load it carries.
The 3.3 V rail, made by the second buck stage.
The quiet 3.3 V rail, made from the 5 V rail by the linear regulator.
A Schottky diode in series: a supply connected the wrong way round is blocked.
A TVS diode across the input: a surge is clamped under what the ICs survive.

One buck stage: the IC with its own circuit (inductor, input and output capacitor banks, the feedback divider, the bootstrap capacitor and the enable divider), a power-good pull-up with its test point, and the power light. `BuckIc` has no power-good pin, but this module names the IC (`Buck<BenchBuck>`), so it joins `BenchBuck`'s `.pg` (ADR 0120).
The IC, a part that provides `BuckIc`.
